ideas.title: Heave! Rock the cart out of its rut
ideas.goal: The cart is stuck in the sand and the player, as Lumi behind it with the friends, gets it out the way people rock a car out of snow: shove, let it roll back into the rut, shove again just as it swings forward. Calling 'heave!' (a key) at the right moment of the swing builds it up until it climbs the berm onto the planks; call too early and everyone pushes against a cart rolling back, the friends land on their faces in the sand. Before the climb the player chooses the wheel width at the carpentry bench: wide boards float on sand but weigh more. Every stuck cart is different (load, rut depth, wet or dry sand), so the rhythm has to be felt each time, and getting it is the satisfying part.
ideas.toward: Road steps 'wheels, axle and frame on a plank track and in sand; the friends push it' and 'the plank road on the dune': the cart moving for the first time, and the measured rolling resistance that later decides how far the charge carries it.
ideas.idea: The swing is not animated: the cart is PrintSim parts on the GPU (a plank frame as an affine body, the three-board wheels on revolute joints) and the rut is the sand field's real shape (sandfield.jl), so the cart rocks because the rut has a slope at both ends and the berm a crest, and each shove that lands on the forward swing adds energy like pushing a swing. Wheels meet the sand by Bekker sinkage per contact cell, which deepens the rut every time it rolls back (so dawdling makes it worse). The friends' bodies really push: their feet are planted on the sand by IK, the body leans until its weight sits behind the frame, and the force each can give is capped by the sand's Mohr-Coulomb shear under its foot's real load (mass x g / foot area, #745); beyond that the foot slips, scoops sand backwards and the friend drops to its belly. Each friend reacts to the call after its own delay, so the crew is a little out of step until the player learns to call early for the slow sheep. A test pushes with 1-6 friends on sand and on planks and records how many shoves it takes, nothing tuned to a number.
ideas.form: Engine part (wheel-sand and foot-sand contact for PrintSim bodies) + a plugin: the stuck cart on the dune, the heave call in Jump in, published; a 540x960 traced short of the crew rocking it free, framed on the cart, the rut and their feet.

ideas.title: Sand fences: build the cart's ramp with the wind
ideas.goal: The cart cannot climb the steep crest, so the player builds the ramp with the wind: plank fences planted on the dune catch the blowing sand, and in front of the player's eyes a drift grows behind each one until it is a slope the cart can take. A fence across the wind builds a ramp, a fence beside the road keeps it clear, a badly placed one buries yesterday's planks. Reading the wind and placing fences is the skill; the road up the dune is the player's own design.
ideas.toward: The dune road the cart drives on (road step 'the plank road on the dune', the cart's climb) and the island's wind measured where it blows: the same solved wind field later turns the windmill, so the generator gets the wind the fences shape.
ideas.idea: The wind is solved, not painted: a horizontal slice of air over the dune runs in WaterLily.jl (an incompressible GPU flow solver on KernelAbstractions, so it can run on Mantle) with every fence, rock, cart and friend as an immersed body given by its signed distance, so wakes, gaps and eddies come from the flow. Where its friction speed at the sand beats Bagnold's threshold the sand field moves grains downwind (Kawamura saltation flux), drops them where the air slows in a wake, and slumps the lee face at the angle of repose. At gale speed it runs in real time: ripples creep, streamers smoke off the crest, a drift builds behind a fence within minutes, a sleeping sheep grows a little tail of sand.
ideas.form: Engine system (WaterLily ground wind + sand transport, live on the dune), fences placed in Jump in, published; a traced short of a drift growing behind a fence into a ramp while the friends watch.
